data.summary: Decision to finish and release ProjectMAPPER. SchemaTOUCHER identified as the active in-progress tool needing completion before release.
data.decision_or_outcome: ProjectMAPPER revival begins. SchemaTOUCHER is the primary build target: a schema-driven record editor backed by a single-file append-only JSONL store called a spine.

data.summary: Core invariants established for SchemaTOUCHER: (1) last registered schema = default working schema on spine open; (2) every entry references its exact schema ID@version; (3) Browse renders each entry under its own recorded schema, independent of the Entry Form active schema.
data.decision_or_outcome: These invariants are non-negotiable and must be preserved across all changes. The three-tab UI (Entry Form / Schema Editor / Browse Entries) is settled and must not be redesigned.

data.summary: Chose single-file JSONL (spine) as the storage format: both schema definitions and data entries live in one ordered stream. The stream is authoritative; the in-memory schema registry is derived from it on open.
data.decision_or_outcome: Rejected: separate schema file + data file (two-file model). Rejected: SQLite. Chosen: single .jsonl with interleaved schema/entry records. Reason: simplicity, portability, human-readability, append-safety.

data.summary: Entry Form / Browse schema isolation decision: the Browse tab must use each entry's recorded schema key to resolve labels, never the Entry Form's currently active schema. Navigating Browse must not change the Entry Form schema.
data.decision_or_outcome: _format_entry_readable() resolves schema from the entry record itself. _browse_prev/_browse_next do not touch _schema_key or _schema_def. Verified by test_browse_navigation_does_not_change_entry_form_schema and test_browse_uses_entry_schema_for_labels.

data.summary: Spine data layer (spine.py) implemented: Spine.create/open/exists, register_schema (immutable versioned schemas), append_entry, read_entries, read_all. SpineError for all failure cases. _iter_records skips malformed/blank lines with log.warning.
data.decision_or_outcome: Record format: schema records have kind=schema, id, version, definition, ts. Entry records have kind=entry, schema (id@version key), ts, data. Schema immutability enforced: re-registering same id@version raises SpineError.

data.summary: SchemaToucherWindow (schema_toucher_ui.py) implemented: three-tab Tkinter UI. Entry Form with scrollable schema-driven form, Entry JSON preview, Append button. Schema Editor with Registered dropdown, text editor, Register button. Browse Entries with Entire Spine / Single Entry / Raw JSONL modes and Prev/Next nav.
data.decision_or_outcome: Field widgets: Entry for strings, Checkbutton for bool, Combobox for enum, Text (5 rows, wrap=word) for textarea fields (format=textarea), Text (3 rows, wrap=none) for object/array fields. _get_value/_set_value/_field_widget are pure helpers testable without a window.

data.summary: textarea field type added after initial implementation. Motivation: prose fields (summaries, notes, descriptions) need multiline plain-string input, not JSON-object input. The existing object/array Text widget parsed its content as JSON, which was wrong for plain prose.
data.decision_or_outcome: Added _is_textarea() check: type=string with format=textarea creates a plain Text widget with _textarea=True marker. _get_value returns raw string (rstrip newline), not JSON-parsed. _set_value inserts str(value) without JSON-encoding. Labelled Browse tab added to show context while browsing.

data.summary: Named spine lifecycle: Spine supports rename() (stem only, .jsonl appended). Spine can be opened from any path (independent location). SchemaToucherWindow supports Spine > Rename Spine menu item. Reopen from a different path works via Spine.open().
data.decision_or_outcome: Spine.rename() updates _path in-place and renames the file. SpineError raised if target exists. SchemaToucherWindow._rename_spine() calls spine.rename() and updates the header. open_schema_toucher() in app.py accepts an optional path= kwarg to open a specific spine on launch.

data.summary: V1 review completed. All 55 tests pass: 24 in test_spine.py, 31 in test_schema_toucher.py. Six checklist items verified: registered schema selector, post-append behavior, draft preservation, whole-spine browsing, readability/integrity, close/move/reopen.
data.decision_or_outcome: No defect fixes required. One gap noted: dirty flag is scaffolded but never set True; close/schema-switch/spine-switch silently discard unappended field data. Decision: park for V1 (low risk for quick-append workflow). V1 accepted.
data.open_questions: Should a 'Clear Form' button or dirty guard be added in V2? Should malformed-line skips be surfaced in the Browse UI (e.g., a status count)?

data.summary: Minimal spine CLI (spine_cli.py) implemented. Four subcommands: init <path>, register <path> --schema <file.json>, append <path> --schema <id@version> --data <file.json>, read <path> [--kind entry|schema|all]. Entry point spine-cli added to pyproject.toml.
data.decision_or_outcome: CLI calls spine.py directly. Errors go to stderr; exit code 1 on failure. read outputs JSONL to stdout (one record per line). Status messages (created/registered/appended) go to stderr. No ambient state, no additional persistence. Round-trip verified: CLI-created spine opens correctly in SchemaTOUCHER. All 55 existing tests still pass.

data.summary: SchemaTOUCHER V1 is complete and accepted. Spine data layer and GUI are fully functional. CLI exposes all four spine operations. This design-session spine demonstrates end-to-end CLI usage.
data.decision_or_outcome: Files: src/projectmapper/tools/spine.py (data layer), src/projectmapper/tools/schema_toucher_ui.py (GUI), src/projectmapper/tools/spine_cli.py (CLI). Tests: tests/test_spine.py (24), tests/test_schema_toucher.py (31). Branch: legacy. Next planned work: V2 improvements (dirty guard, Clear Form, malformed-line UI notice) and eventual merge to main for release.
data.open_questions: Should V2 be started on a separate branch? Are there additional schemas or use cases to validate before merge to main? Is the three-tab layout final for release or subject to UX review?

data.summary:
Spine as connective tissue: key project documents and their spine references.

Design decisions → .spine/schematoucher-design.jsonl (this file)
Backlog (Tier A/B/C items) → docs/backlog.md
Repair sprint plan → docs/plans/2026-10-30-repair-sprint.md
Adversarial complexity review → memory/project-complexity-review.md
V1 acceptance criteria → docs/acceptance/v1.1.0.md
Developer guide → docs/developer-guide.md

Convention: each design spine entry that references a doc names the doc path relative to the project root. A fresh assistant given this spine + codebase snapshot should be able to reconstruct project context without reading every file.
data.decision_or_outcome: Established the pattern: spine entries reference docs by path; docs/backlog.md is now the canonical list of parked work.
data.open_questions: Should the spine also track external references (e.g. session transcripts, review session IDs)? That would let the spine serve as the single recovery point for any conversation that needs full project history.

data.summary:
Established session_ref convention for spine entries.

When an entry records a decision or implementation tied to a specific conversation, include a session_ref field with the Claude Code session ID. This lets a future assistant trace the reasoning behind a decision by looking up the transcript, not just reading what was decided.
data.decision_or_outcome:
session_ref: 38159a69-c603-4da0-aa85-edfcc949dead

Convention applies going forward to all spine appends where the entry is tied to a conversation. Saved to memory as feedback-spine-session-refs.md.

data.summary:
Added onboarding section to docs/README.md.

The section tells a fresh assistant or contributor where to start: this file → developer-guide → backlog → spine → acceptance record. The spine entry in the README describes the design-event@1 schema (fields, event_type enum, session_ref convention) and names the last recorded state, so the README itself works as a manifest of schema and current position in the spine.
data.decision_or_outcome: docs/README.md updated. The spine is now self-describing from the README: a reader does not need to open the .jsonl to understand its schema or know where the journal currently stands.

data.summary: Public sidecar release: jacobmentalconstruct/.project-mapper. Clone as .project-mapper/ into any project. Fresh git history, no dev materials.
data.decision_or_outcome: Repo live at https://github.com/jacobmentalconstruct/.project-mapper (commit 04cb318). 10/10 cold-clone checks passed. Two fix commits applied post-initial: (1) screenshot filenames shortened for Windows MAX_PATH compatibility; (2) pyproject.toml Repository URL corrected to public repo. SIDECAR_ROOT_NAME=.project-mapper, detection updated (no app/ subdir), .project-mapper added to EXCLUDED_FOLDERS.

data.summary: Main window UI cleanup: file picker bar removed, settings exposed as gear icon. In sidecar mode the root is auto-detected so the picker row (label, entry, Choose, Up buttons) is unnecessary. selected_root_var StringVar retained for programmatic root changes.
data.decision_or_outcome: Gear button initially placed as floating overlay (place()), then redesigned by sibling session to a compact packed header frame: project name bold left, full path muted, gear tucked right (commit b462e6b). 501 tests pass.

data.summary: Fixed UTF-8 BOM stripping in spine JSONL reader (commit d175563). Entries written by some tools included a BOM prefix that caused JSON parse failures.
data.decision_or_outcome: Reader now strips BOM before parsing each line.
